web.title: Katori Minar: Kitty Party Game Rules, How to Play and Twists
web.description: Katori Minar is a one minute kitty party game where ladies stack steel katoris, glasses and dabbas with one hand. Learn what you need, steps, rules and twists.
web.intro: Katori Minar is a one minute kitty party stacking game where every lady builds the tallest tower she can from 10 steel katoris, glasses and small dabbas, using only one hand. Whoever has the tallest tower still standing when the timer ends wins the round, and round winners play a final. The crazy twist: twice in the minute the host rings a steel glass and shouts "Doorbell!", and every lady must stand up, turn around once, say "Aayi ji!" and sit back down before she can add another piece. It needs nothing but kitchen utensils and a phone timer.
materials: 10 steel utensils per lady in the round: a mix of katoris, steel glasses and small dabbas with lids
A table, or a clean patch of floor
A phone timer set to 1 minute
One steel glass and a spoon for the host to ring as the doorbell
steps: Play in rounds of 4 or 5 ladies. Give each lady 10 steel utensils (katoris, glasses and small dabbas) in a heap in front of her on the table.
Every lady puts one hand behind her back. When the host starts the 1 minute timer, she builds a tower with her other hand, placing one utensil at a time, mouth up or mouth down as she likes.
If a tower falls, that lady must start again from the bottom with her first piece. The timer does not stop for her.

Twice during the minute the host rings the steel glass with a spoon and shouts "Doorbell!". Every lady must let go, stand up, turn around once, say "Aayi ji!" and sit down before adding her next piece.
When the timer ends, all hands come off. The tallest tower still standing wins the round, with the piece count as the tie breaker. Round winners then play one final round for the prize.
rules: Using the second hand makes that tower count as zero for the round.
A lady who does not stand up on "Doorbell!" must take one utensil off her tower.
Touching the tower after the timer ends means she is out.
Only towers still standing at the end are measured.
Use steel utensils only, never glass or anything fragile.
variations: Let each lady blow on her neighbour's tower once during the minute, without touching it.
In the final, every lady must build with her non dominant hand.
Ring the doorbell three times in the last 20 seconds for a chaotic finish.
tips: Keep the table clear of plates and drinks so a falling tower lands safely.
Mouth down katoris make a steady base; save the glasses for the top.
Put the same mix of utensils in front of every lady so each round is fair.
Play on a rug or a mat if you use the floor, to keep the noise down.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Katori Minar?
faq.a: It works for 8 to 20 ladies. Play in rounds of 4 or 5 at a time so you have enough utensils, then let the round winners play a final.

faq.q: What do you need to play Katori Minar?
faq.a: About 10 steel utensils per lady in a round (katoris, steel glasses, small dabbas), a table or clean floor, a phone timer and one steel glass with a spoon for the doorbell.

faq.q: How long does the game take?
faq.a: Each round is just 1 minute, so the whole game with 3 or 4 rounds and a final takes 10 to 15 minutes.

faq.q: Is Katori Minar safe to play at a kitty party?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you use only steel utensils and keep glassware, hot dishes and drinks off the table. A falling tower just makes a loud clang.

faq.q: Is Katori Minar a good one minute game for ladies?
faq.a: Yes. It needs no prep, everyone already knows how to stack katoris, and the Doorbell twist keeps the whole room laughing even when towers fall.
